# PROCESS — what I did this iteration (explainability; REQUIRED)

Candidate cand_0001, iteration 1 of 3, EMPTY seed (prompt.md was 0 bytes, no task_template.md). Baseline val 0.450 (18/40). Diagnosed all 22 failures by reading each trace (/tmp/trc1) and diffing the output against the init and golden workbooks with openpyxl. Scoring: hard, REWARD_RECALC=0, so the grader reads the saved file with data_only=True and does no recalculation. All 22 rollouts had error=None, so there is no infra noise.

## Ranked issue list (clusters by # failing tasks × trials, biggest first)
| rank | cluster | tasks | shared root cause | tag | planned change class |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| 1 | A. Formula string written, logic right | 37378, 46897, 53383, 55049, 6698, 7902, 8942 (7) | Agent writes `ws[c] = "=..."`. Without recalc the cell reads None, so it scores 0 even though the formula is correct. Questions say "I need a formula", and the agent takes that literally. | KNOWLEDGE (grading contract) | CONTRACT: write computed literal values; explain WHY (no recalc) |
| 2 | B. Formula written AND wrong/unevaluable | 37456, 53647, 54144, 56563, 9569, 55979 (6) | Same habit, plus complex SUMPRODUCT/AGGREGATE logic that is wrong or would not evaluate. Computing in Python forces the agent to get concrete values (e.g. 56563 must skip '#NUM!' strings; 55979 needs exact sheet-name text 'Supplier_1'). | KNOWLEDGE + BEHAVIORAL | CONTRACT plus edge-case knowledge (error strings are str, exact text) |
| 3 | E. Misread layout / semantics | 59196, 39046, 43436, 48527, 51-12 (5) | Relied on the pandas preview, which hides an empty row 1 (59196: headers are in row 2). Did not use the worked examples in the sheet (51-12: row 2 shows the expected marker count; 39046: existing helper columns). | BEHAVIORAL | WORKFLOW: inspect cells with coordinates via openpyxl; treat in-sheet examples as test cases |
| 4 | D. pandas round-trip damage | 227-40, 50768, 48527, 80-42 (4) | `read_excel`/`to_excel` shifted the header row, overwrote existing cells (50768 F14), and dropped sheets. | KNOWLEDGE | WORKFLOW: openpyxl load-modify-save of the original; pandas is fine for computing only |
| 5 | C. Existing formulas in answer cells | 267-18 (also 43436) | Re-saving with openpyxl drops cached values, so untouched formula cells in answer_position read None (267-18 G1). | KNOWLEDGE | CONTRACT: overwrite answer cells that hold formulas with literal values from data_only |
| 6 | F. No verification / looping | cross-cutting (37456, 9569 and others: identical code resent, silent runs, default template says "once that file exists, you are done") | No feedback loop. The adapter grants 3 verify rounds after the first write, but the template discourages using them. | BEHAVIORAL | TEMPLATE: explicit Inspect → Solve → Verify steps; "print, never resend the same code" |

## Changes made this iteration
| cluster | edit class | file / tool | what & why it generalizes | protects passing? |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| A, B, C | CONTRACT | prompt.md "How your output is judged" | Explains that the grader opens with data_only and does not recalc, so formula strings read empty. Rule: compute in Python and write values, even for "I need a formula" or VBA requests. Answer cells that already hold formulas get literal values. | Yes. Of the 18 passes, 10 have formula goldens (12864, 2768, 38462, 45635, 47798, 48588, 48620, 48921, 59595, 9726) and ALL passed by writing values, so this codifies what they already do. |
| B | KNOWLEDGE | prompt.md | Type-sensitive comparison (numbers as int/float, exact text such as sheet names, empty means None). Error strings '#N/A'/'#NUM!' are str and should be skipped where AGGREGATE/IFERROR would. | Yes. It is advisory and matches the passing outputs, which are numeric. |
| E | BEHAVIORAL (workflow) | prompt.md step 1-2 + task_template field description | The preview hides leading empty rows and renames headers, so print the real cells with coordinates. Use in-sheet examples and any pre-filled answer cells as test cases. | Yes. It only adds an inspection round, and the 30-turn budget is ample (passing runs use 2-6 rounds). |
| D | KNOWLEDGE (workflow) | prompt.md step 4 | Prefer openpyxl load-modify-save of the original; pandas for computation only; check row offsets. Worded as "prefer", not "forbid". | MODERATE risk. 14 passing tasks used pandas to_excel. They may switch to openpyxl, which is strictly safer for the cell positions. I did not forbid pandas. |
| F | BEHAVIORAL (interaction contract) | task_template.md (replaced the "once that file exists, you are done" line) | Three numbered steps (Inspect / Solve / Verify), told that only a few rounds remain after the file exists (matches VERIFY_TURNS=3), and finish with a no-code reply (the adapter then stops cleanly). | Yes. All placeholders are kept, and `_task_template_error()` returns None (checked by importing the adapter). |

## Verify-the-fix
- 37378 trace: `ws[f'A{row}'] = '=IF(B{row}<>"", COUNTA($B$2:B{row}), "")'`. The new contract says this reads None and to compute COUNTA in Python. The logic is already right, so values follow.
- 9569 trace round 1 (repeated in round 3): the agent reasons "the prompt says 'I need a formula'. Let's use openpyxl to write the formula", then writes AGGREGATE formulas, and the output is empty. The prompt now addresses exactly this sentence ("even when the user's question says 'I need a formula'"). Python "first non-zero in E:AN" is trivial.
- 267-18: G1 is a formula in init, and it was re-saved without a cache, so None. The new rule is to read data_only and write the literal into every answer cell, including the unchanged G1.
- 59196: headers are in D2:G2 with row 1 empty, and the preview hid this. Step 1 now says to print coordinates and states that the header may be in row 2 or lower.
- 50768 / 227-40: the to_excel round-trip shifted the header and clobbered F14. Step 4 now says to use openpyxl load-modify-save and to set only the answer cells.
- 51-12: row 2 holds the worked example of markers 1–4. Step 2 says to treat in-sheet examples as test cases.
- 56563: the sum must skip '#NUM!' strings. The knowledge line names exactly this.
- F (all): template step 3 tells the agent to reopen with data_only and print. A None or formula string then becomes visible to the agent within the 3 verify rounds.

## Process & features used
- Subagents / worktrees / parallel features used: none. This was a serial fallback because the session instructions say not to call the Agent tool or workflows unless the user requested it. Diagnosis used local helper scripts (/tmp/sb/show.py: init vs golden cell values and formulas per range; trace dumps in /tmp/trc1).
- Prior iterations read: none exist (RUNMAP empty, rejected.jsonl empty, LEDGER has no rows).
- Template validity was checked with `adapter._task_template_error(cand_dir)`, which returned None.

## Good things to PRESERVE
- The "write literal values, the grader does not recalc" contract and its WHY. This is the single largest lever (13 of 22 failures write formulas).
- The Verify step in task_template.md, which replaces "once that file exists, you are done".
- All 6 required placeholders plus {max_turns} in task_template.md.

## Deliberately skipped
- No task-specific hints (e.g. 39046 "Yes if REF appears more than once", 48527 "first non-No text"). Those would be hardcoding. The generic "use in-sheet examples as test cases" rule is the general form.
- 43436 / 48527 / 80-42 semantic errors beyond the layout issues may remain unsolved. They need better question interpretation, which a prompt can only nudge.
- No prompt.md length bloat: the model is a frontier tier, so I kept the prompt to the WHY plus a 5-step workflow.

---

# DIAGNOSIS.json — machine-readable diagnosis (OPTIONAL but recommended)

In addition to PROCESS.md, you may write a DIAGNOSIS.json file to make your diagnosis machine-readable for the dashboard. This is optional; if absent, the dashboard will parse PROCESS.md tables when present, or show only outcome data.

The schema:
```json
{
  "candidate": "cand_NNNN",
  "headline": "Brief summary of this iteration's strategy",
  "clusters": [
    {"id": "A", "name": "Short cluster name",
     "detail": "Root cause explanation", "tasks": ["task-id", ...],
     "scope": "BOUNDED|WIDESPREAD|SYSTEMIC", "latent": false,
     "tag": "KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|CAPABILITY-GAP"}
  ],
  "edits": [
    {"id": "E1", "title": "What this edit does",
     "files": ["prompt.md"], "lever": "CONTRACT|KNOWLEDGE|BEHAVIORAL|...",
     "clusters": ["A"], "blast_radius": "BOUNDED|MODERATE|WIDE",
     "verified": "How you tested it"}
  ],
  "skipped": [{"title": "What was skipped", "reason": "Why"}],
  "techniques": ["technique 1", "technique 2"]
}
```

Validation is advisory only and never blocks an iteration. Warnings are recorded when:
- A task ID in clusters[].tasks is not in the val split
- An edit references a cluster ID that does not exist
- An edit references a file that does not exist in the candidate
